sentences.text: HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard the arguments from both the counsel.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award passed in MVC No.166/2022 dated 30.10.2023 by the Court of Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Kollegal.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Kollegal

sentences.text: 3. The injured claimant, who is aged 16 years, has met with an accident on 14.03.2022 and filed the claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, has awarded the compensation of Rs.3,27,360/- with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till the date of realization.
4. Aggrieved by the said order, the present appeal is preferred.

In which, it is contended that as per the evidence of CW.1 - doctor and Wound Certificate at Ex.P6, the claimant has sustained fracture of left humorous and surgery was also done, but the compensation granted under the heads 'pain and suffering' and 'discomfort, NC: 2026:KHC:201 HC-KAR inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents' is on lower side.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to enhance the compensation.
The Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head 'discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents', which is on the lower side.

The same is enhanced to Rs.45,000/.
5.

Thus, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation :
 SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT  (IN.RS.)
1. Pain and suffering. 3,00,000.00  2. Discomfort, inconvenience 45,000.00  and loss of earning to the  parents during the period of  hospitalization  3.
Medical expenses 2,360.00  4.
Future medical expenses 15,000.00  Total 3,62,362.00  Less: the respondent paid Rs.5,000 5,000.00  which is to be deducted  Payable 3,57,360 6.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.3,27,360/- but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.3,57,360/-.

Therefore, the NC: 2026:KHC:201 HC-KAR appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.30,000/- (Rs.3,57,360 - Amuda S vs The Divisional Controller on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142696767/
2 Rs.3,27,360) along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
